subject: Thresholds and backstop billing for AtlasHealth POC
messages:
From: Claire Huang <claire@atlashealth.ai>
To: karthik_iyer@redwood.com, ben_carter@redwood.com
Cc: procurement@atlashealth.ai
Date: Sun, 12 Sep 2027 09:14:00 -0700
Subject: Thresholds and backstop billing for AtlasHealth POC

Hi Karthik / Ben,

Thanks again for the demo last week — Atlas is excited to move into a 3-month POC. Before we finalize the SOW, procurement needs clarity on two billing items:

1) Minimum spend definition for hosted API commits — is this a monthly committed token spend or an annualized floor?
2) On-demand / burst over-commit pricing — what rate applies when we exceed the committed monthly volume for short spikes? Do you have a backstop cap to prevent runaway bills?

Quick context: our engineering forecasts show a base of ~1.2B tokens/month with infrequent spikes to ~3–3.5B for short windows. For the POC we can commit to a 1.0B monthly floor if the burst policy is reasonable.

Can you send a concise pricing table + example invoices for a few scenarios (monthly true-up, a 30% spike, a 200% spike)? I attached our internal high-level volume forecast for reference (not required in your materials).

Thanks — happy to jump on a short call if easier.

— Claire
Claire Huang
Head of Data Products | AtlasHealth
claire@atlashealth.ai
+1 (415) 555-0199

Attachments referenced: Atlas_Volume_Forecast_Sept2027.xlsx (attached by Claire)

From: karthik_iyer@redwood.com
To: Claire Huang <claire@atlashealth.ai>
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.com, vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com
Date: Sun, 12 Sep 2027 13:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Thresholds and backstop billing for AtlasHealth POC

Hi Claire — thanks for the clear context, and excited to partner on the POC. Attached are two things: (1) Pricing_Table_20270912.xlsx (detailed per-token rates and worked examples) and (2) Atlas_SOW_Draft_v2.pdf (POC scope + sign-off).

High-level options (short bullets so you can share with procurement):
- Commit model: monthly committed tokens (e.g., 1.0B/mo) billed at committed per-token rate. Unused committed tokens do not carry forward.
- Monthly true-up: at month-end we net actual usage vs commit; if actual > commit, overage billed at on-demand overage rate.
- Overage structure (recommended for POC):
  * First 20% over commit: billed at 1.4x list on-demand per-token rate (soft buffer for small spikes).
  * 20%–200% over commit (i.e., up to ~3x): billed at 1.6x list on-demand per-token rate.
  * >200% of commit: active throttling/fallback to queued requests or best-effort model; we can enable emergency burst at 2.2x list for a capped number of tokens per hour if you opt-in.
- Backstop / runaway protection: we can put a daily cap (tokens/hour) and an automated alerting + manual approval flow for anything likely to exceed 3x in a 24-hour window.

Alternate: if Atlas prefers predictability, we can structure a soft floor (monthly minimum charge equal to 60% of committed dollars) plus a reduced overage multiplier (1.5x) with a 30-day true-up and an early usage review after 60 days.

Let me know which path procurement prefers. If you want, Ben and I can create two SOW variations (Hard-commit + soft-burst vs Soft-floor + blended overage) and route for signature.

Best,
Karthik Iyer
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
karthik_iyer@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0123

From: vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com

Date: Mon, 13 Sep 2027 11:20:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Thresholds and backstop billing for AtlasHealth POC

Looping in finance perspective. Karthik — thanks for the clear options. A few clarifying notes and a suggested guardrail:

> From Karthik: "First 20% over commit: billed at 1.4x... 20%–200%: billed at 1.6x... >200%: throttling / emergency 2.2x"

- Define minimum spend precisely: we recommend "monthly committed token spend" (dollars) billed each month regardless of consumption for POC. We should avoid annualizing for a short trial.
- We should add a 30-day retro credit cap: if true-up shows overbilling relative to forecasted product behavior, customer may request a single 30-day adjustment review per quarter (requires supporting logs).
- For Atlas specifically: given expected spikes, propose a tiered overage with sharper gradation to protect both sides: 0–20% = 1.35x, 20–75% = 1.55x, 75–200% = 1.85x, >200% = manual approval/emergency burst at 2.25x with hourly cap. This reduces sticker shock for small spikes while protecting capacity planning.
- Include a short clause: "Emergency bursts are consented and may be rate-limited; charges for bursts will not be refunded unless capacity-event is caused by Redwood outage."

Ben — please advise on whether we want to offer a one-time 60-day minimum-waiver for new logos to accelerate signature.

Vivek Kulkarni
Director, Revenue Ops | Redwood Inference
vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com

From: ben_carter@redwood.com
To: Claire Huang <claire@atlashealth.ai>, karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Cc: vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 14 Sep 2027 10:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Thresholds and backstop billing for AtlasHealth POC

Claire — appreciate the candor. Proposed commercial compromise (for the POC only):

- Commit: Atlas signs a 1.0B token/mo commit for the 3-month POC.
- Overage: blended overage approach so invoices are predictable: we will compute overage as a weighted blend that targets an effective 1.5x on-demand multiplier across typical spike profiles. Practically: 0–30% = 1.35x, 30–150% = 1.6x, >150% = 2.0x (emergency burst opt-in required).
- True-up: monthly true-up with 30-day invoice adjustment window; finance review allowed once per quarter.
- One-time onboarding concession: first month we can cap overage charges to 1.2x for the first 500M burst tokens as a goodwill credit (to let your engineers tune).

If that reads OK, Karthik — can you prepare two SOWs (one that includes the goodwill credit and one without) and route the DocuSign link? I'll approve the credit from my side if legal signs off.

Best,
Ben Carter
VP, Sales | Redwood Inference
